title: How Manhunts Work
summary: Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Noel) explore how manhunts work, using historical and recent cases: James Earl Ray's escape after the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr. and his capture at Heathrow; Whitey Bulger's years on the lam and the FBI TV appeals; John Wilkes Booth; the Boston Marathon bombing manhunt, including the lockdown, containment, and the boat search; the Christopher Dorner manhunt in Los Angeles; the Osama bin Laden operation and the fake vaccination drive; the Unabomber, found by his brother; Eric Robert Rudolph; and the role of social media, Reddit, and crowdsourcing. They also cover containment and door-to-door searches, and the legal limits on police entering homes (probable cause, exigent circumstances, emergency aid). The episode ends with a listener email about chess rules and castling.

segments.title: Opening banter and James Earl Ray
segments.summary: Hosts open the show and introduce manhunts through James Earl Ray's escape after the King assassination, including his forged passport and capture at Heathrow, and the later confession and death in prison.

segments.title: Whitey Bulger and famous fugitives
segments.summary: Discussion of fugitives who hid for long periods, including Whitey Bulger's years on the lam and the FBI's TV appeals that led to his girlfriend's tip, and John Wilkes Booth's brief flight.

segments.title: Public involvement as a manhunt principle
segments.summary: The hosts say that getting the public involved and having many people do grunt work are common features of successful manhunts.

segments.title: Containment and door-to-door searches
segments.summary: Explanation of containment, sealing off an area and watching exits, and door-to-door searches for a regional manhunt.

segments.title: Boston Marathon bombing manhunt
segments.summary: Overview of the Boston manhunt: release of suspect photos, the shootout, the lockdown and shelter-in-place order, the boat search found with infrared imaging, and the homeowner who called police.

segments.title: Police entry into homes and legal limits
segments.summary: Discussion of when police can enter homes without consent, including probable cause, exigent circumstances, and emergency aid, and how improper searches can undermine a case.

segments.title: Christopher Dorner and collateral damage
segments.summary: The Los Angeles manhunt for former LAPD officer Christopher Dorner, the shootings of two innocent people, and his death in a cabin fire, along with the idea of collateral damage.

segments.title: Bin Laden hunt and modern surveillance tools
segments.summary: Discussion of the bin Laden search, including the fake immunization drive for DNA and its backlash, plus modern tools like cameras, infrared, drones and armored vehicles, and facial recognition.

segments.title: Social media, Reddit, and famous long manhunts
segments.summary: Reddit's crowdsourced photo sleuthing in Boston and its backlash, the Unabomber case solved with help from his brother, Eric Robert Rudolph, Richard Jewell, and online crowdsourced manhunts.
